title: A Pathetic MMO
paragraphs: I consider Ren’s opinion as well.
If I recall correctly… Wasn’t it enough to have a dragon ingest a fragment of the Dragon Emperor?
“If the fragment of the Dragon Emperor is in the core of the dragon we defeated, then there may be no issue. But I’m not sure if we can persuade them. And besides, I was asked last time.”
“Uh, do you mean that, like with Naofumi-san, someone left you a message or request before the loop?”
I nod at Itsuki’s words. His sharp intuition is a great help.
“Exactly!”
“Seriously… You should have mentioned that sooner!”
“This is a complete waste of effort… Wait, now that I think about it, isn’t it impossible for us to stay in Melromarc after causing such a huge commotion?”
Father slumps in exasperation.
“Not to mention, Faubrey is right in front of us…”
“It would be best if we took care of this now.”
“Why?”
“Because it will help us exterminate the enemies infesting Faubrey.”

Better safe than sorry. Thinking back, Takt’s dragon gave us a lot of trouble in the previous loop. In the first world and when we went to Siltvelt, we managed to defeat it easily, but we can’t say for sure that it won’t resurrect. That thing even turned into a dragon zombie.
Should we be persuading some dragon somewhere?
“Besides, the enemy’s followers were a huge pain for me and Father two loops ago.”
There’s also a chance it could evolve into an imperial dragon.
If that happens, who knows how much of a hassle it’ll become?
“So basically, we should think of it as an enemy that requires specific conditions to be defeated…?”
“That’s correct.”
“I see, I’ve heard of things like that in games and mythology.”
“Like when solid and liquid attacks don’t work, right? I remember something like that too.”
“Oh, one of those enemies that are an instant death trap for first-timers, huh…”
“If things go well, I believe we can take it down. However, we can’t predict what will happen in Faubrey, so I think we should prepare in advance.”

Even if we defeat Takt’s Dragon Emperor and store its fragments… can we really say for sure they won’t be misused? It’s not just the remnants. A Dragon Emperor can be used as a powerful material, and if a country takes possession of it and it gets stolen, that would be troublesome. But if we incorporate it into a weapon, extracting it later would be a major ordeal. Preparation is key.
“Got it. I don’t know what’s going to happen, but heading to Faubrey now is dangerous, right, Motoyasu?”
“That’s right. Ideally, we should strengthen that rival to a certain extent before making our move.”
“Why?”
“It seems that Dragon Emperors have a tendency to collect core stones. And they can also take over other dragons.”
“Ah, I see. Then we definitely need to power up beforehand, or it could get really dangerous. There’s a risk that the dragon we’re supposed to defeat could end up being taken over by an ally.”
Father is quick to understand, which is a great help. At that moment, Éclair raises her hand.
“Hmm… In that case, would it be possible to check on Father’s territory at the same time?”
“Ah… Yeah, I’m curious about what happened to Eclair-san’s father’s territory too. I mean… we did cause quite a bit of chaos.”
“Perhaps this timing isn’t too bad after all. Fortunately, there’s hardly any threats left that could harm us, and even though it’s enemy territory, if it’s necessary, we should go.”
“Then it’s decided.”
“Where are we going?”
Sakura tilts her head in curiosity.
“From the conversation, it sounds like we’re going to a country called Melromarc, right?”
“Departure~?”
Koh excitedly asks.
“That’s right. But since we don’t know what might happen, let’s take it easy today and leave tomorrow.”
“Understood.”

And so, just as we were about to enter Faubrey, we decided to head to Melromarc instead. Come to think of it, there were still many things in Melromarc that we hadn’t collected yet. It wouldn’t be a bad idea to take care of the Waves quickly while we’re there. For the sake of the world. --- The next morning. Just as we were about to reach the borders of Faubrey, I used a portal to take Father and the others back to Melromarc. At first, I was going to teleport directly to the castle garden, but after being warned by Father and the others, I instead transported us to a village in Melromarc.
“So this is Melromarc…? Wait, that sounds weird considering it’s the country that summoned us… I should already know it, shouldn’t I?”
“We were only here for a little over two days and stayed near the castle town. I think it’s fair to say it’s still an unfamiliar country to us.”
“Yeah. If this were a game, I’d remember what kind of monsters are around and where the towns are, but…”
“That’s mostly accurate. However, unlike a game, there are slightly more towns and villages here.”
“…That’s probably why Itsuki and I ended up perceiving this world as just another game.”
“Yes. By the way… We should remain on guard for any assassins targeting us, right?”
“I doubt it. We teleported in using a portal, after all.”
“I think so too. Of course, it never hurts to stay cautious.”
It’s a peaceful rural village, with the morning sun just beginning to rise.
Now then, how long will it take to reach my rival from here?
“So, Motoyasu. Where exactly is your destination?”
“I’m sure Ren can figure it out.”
“Huh?”
Ren looks at me with a dumbfounded expression. It’s a place Ren often visited and caused trouble in every loop. It must have been the same in the first world as well.
“Ren-san, when Motoyasu-san says things like this, it usually involves problems you caused in the first world… something related to your game knowledge, perhaps?”
“Even if you say that out of nowhere…”
“Isn’t it something related to dragons? Didn’t some quests or events in the game involve them in a significant way?”
“Now that you mention it, I do recall something. There was a quest where you could start by hunting dragons as a foothold.”
“That’s probably it. If the level gain was good, you might have fought them just for the drops or materials.”
“Indeed. My goal is to convince that dragon and recruit it.”
“You can do something like that…?”
“It’s kind of like those online games where you can recruit field bosses as allies, either because the developers ran out of ideas or thought it would be an interesting feature.”

Hmm, Father sure knows a lot about these things. Though there was a hint of sarcasm in his tone. Come to think of it, I remember hearing about a subpar MMO that heavily advertised its generic mount system as if it were groundbreaking. Judging by Father’s tone, I sense a similar kind of sarcasm.
“I haven’t played nearly as many games as Naofumi, so I don’t know much, but… does that really exist?”
“It seems so.”
From their reactions, it looks like Itsuki doesn’t know about it either.
“By the way, when Ren killed this dragon back then and left its corpse behind, the nearby villagers turned it into a tourist attraction. But then, the body rotted and caused a plague to spread.”
“…What?”
“Wait… does that mean…?”
“H-hold on, are you saying people died because of me?”
Ren’s face is turning pale.
What’s he acting so shocked about now?

“If I remember correctly, Ren’s excuse was that it was the fault of the people who left the corpse there, right? You claimed you left it behind for the benefit of regular adventurers, or something along those lines.”
“And as a result, a plague spread… I’m surprised the version of me from the first world let you off the hook.”
“From what I heard, Father was the one who resolved the issue. Besides, you had your own conflicts to deal with at the time, so maybe you didn’t have the chance to call Ren out on it?”
“I-I see… Perhaps, rather than seeing Ren-san as the villain, I was more focused on blaming Naofumi-san back then.”
“I-I’ll be extra careful from now on. If I caused that in the first world, I need to make sure I don’t repeat the same mistake.”
Ren at least has a sense of responsibility, so that should be enough to prevent a repeat of that disaster. Oh, while we’re at it, I should explain another thing.
“By the way, this dragon—whom I refer to as ‘Assistant’—has an adopted demi-human child. And this Assistant seems to hold quite the grudge against Ren.”
“Wait, if they’re adopted, doesn’t that mean… Ren basically ended up killing their parent?”
Father carefully chooses his words while looking back and forth between me and Ren.
“Uh… ah… ugh…”
Ren, despite not having committed the act yet in this timeline, is already turning even paler.
Is he really unable to just dismiss it as someone else’s problem?
